What readers see when they hit a paywall

We spent a month collecting the messages that news sites show when a reader runs out of free articles, and the wording turned out to be remarkably uniform. Most of them say some version of "Subscribe to continue reading", usually above a button and a price, and a surprising number add a countdown or a discount that expires at midnight to hurry the decision along.

Smaller sites tend to be more personal. One regional title we looked at tells readers that "this article is for subscribers only" and then explains, in a paragraph of its own, how many reporters the subscriptions pay for, while a newsletter we follow says the post is for paid members only and offers a free week instead of a discount.

None of this is new, but the convergence matters for anyone building tools that read the news. A reader app that cannot tell a gate from an article will happily show a teaser as if it were the whole story, which is worse for the reader than showing a headline and a link.
